title: B2+ · L22 — Metaphors & figurative language
description: Reconocer y construir metaforas en ingles: life is a journey, dead metaphors, y figurative language para argumentar y persuadir.

questions.prompt: En clase de literatura tu profesor analiza el famoso lema atribuido a Benjamin Franklin.
questions.question: In 'Time is money', what type of figurative device is used?
options: Metaphor — X is Y without any comparison marker.
Personification — giving human traits to abstract concepts.
questions.explanation: Metafora = afirmar que X ES Y sin marcador de comparacion ('like'/'as'). Aqui el tiempo se equipara conceptualmente al dinero: se 'invierte', se 'gasta', se 'ahorra', se 'pierde'. Base de la Conceptual Metaphor Theory de Lakoff & Johnson (1980), fundamental en linguistica cognitiva. Error hispano tipico: confundir con simil porque en espanol 'metafora' se usa a veces coloquialmente para cualquier comparacion — en anglo academico la distincion es rigurosa y examinable.
examples: Life is a journey. → metafora conceptual clasica (LIFE IS A JOURNEY)
The mind is a machine. → metafora que ha moldeado toda la psicologia cognitiva moderna

questions.prompt: Tu estudiante te pregunta la diferencia entre metaphor y simile en su ensayo literario.
questions.question: What is a 'simile'?
questions.explanation: Simile = comparacion EXPLICITA con 'like' o 'as': 'brave as a lion', 'runs like the wind'. Metafora omite el marcador. La distincion es cruciera para literary analysis en anglo (aparece en cada A-level y AP English exam). Colocacion tipica: 'as + adjective + as + noun' (as busy as a bee) o 'verb + like + noun' (fights like a warrior). Error hispano frecuente: usar 'as' donde nativos usarian 'like' — 'she cries as a baby' es incorrecto; correcto: 'she cries like a baby'.
examples: She was as busy as a bee all afternoon — didn't stop for a single second. → simile de actividad
He fights like a warrior when he's defending his ideas in meetings. → simile de caracter

questions.statement: 'The kettle is boiling' is a dead metaphor — used so often that we no longer notice the metaphor.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Dead metaphors = expresiones originalmente metaforicas que se han lexicalizado hasta hacerse invisibles. Literalmente el agua hierve, no la tetera; pero nadie lo procesa como metafora al escucharlo. Otros ejemplos canonicos: 'leg of the table', 'foot of the mountain', 'heart of the city', 'face of a clock', 'mouth of a river'. Concepto esencial en linguistica cognitiva (Lakoff): la mayoria de nuestro lenguaje es metafora muerta. Registro: analisis academico literario.
examples: 'Foot of the mountain' — mountains have no feet, but the metaphor died centuries ago. → dead metaphor topografico
'The heart of the city' — cities have no organs, but this feels literal to us now. → metafora corporal fosilizada

questions.prompt: Analizas la letra de una cancion romantica clasica para tu grupo de lectura.
questions.question: In 'She's the sunshine of my life', 'sunshine' functions as:
options: A metaphor for joy, warmth, or brightness.
A physical light source in the room.
A simile comparing her to weather.
questions.explanation: Metafora conceptual: PERSON IS SUNSHINE (persona positiva como fuente de calor y luz). Extremadamente comun en canciones (Stevie Wonder), discursos amorosos, cartas. Se basa en la asociacion universal luz = alegria (metafora conceptual embodied — Lakoff). Colocacion tipica: 'X is my sunshine/light/star/rock'. Error hispano: intentar traducir literal 'ella es el rayo de sol de mi vida' funciona, pero suena mas pomposo en espanol que en anglo, donde estas metaforas son cotidianas.
examples: You're the light of my life — genuinely, don't know what I'd do without you. → metafora amorosa clasica
My kids are my whole world — everything else is background noise. → metafora de prioridades

questions.text: Her career took off like a rocket after that breakthrough — everything just fell into place.
questions.explanation: Combina simile ('took off like a rocket') + idiom/dead metaphor ('fell into place'). Fenomeno de connected speech: 'took off' con /kf/ cluster, en habla rapida se elide la /f/ final dejando /tʊkɒf/. 'Fell into' se enlaza como /felɪntə/ con schwa. 'Fall into place' es dead metaphor visualmente clara (piezas de puzzle encajando). Colocacion nativa: 'take off' aplicado a carreras, negocios, tendencias es ubicuo. Error hispano: 'take off' se traduce como 'despegar', no 'sacar'.
examples: The idea spread like wildfire on Twitter — three million views in 24 hours. → simile viral
Everything clicked once we changed the approach — should have done it months ago. → dead metaphor mental

questions.prompt: Repasas recursos figurativos con tu grupo antes del examen.
questions.question: Which is 'personification'?
options: The act of buying or selling a person.
Giving human qualities to non-human things.
questions.explanation: Personificacion = atribuir cualidades humanas (acciones, emociones, intenciones) a objetos, conceptos abstractos o fenomenos naturales. Ejemplos canonicos: 'Time waits for no one', 'Opportunity knocks', 'The wind whispered through the trees', 'Fear gripped her'. Recurso central en poesia, publicidad, discurso emocional. Registro: neutro-literario. Error hispano: confundir con 'personalizacion' (adaptar a alguien) — son cosas distintas.
examples: The clock stared at me from the wall as if daring me to leave. → tiempo hostil
Fear gripped her the moment she saw the email subject line. → emocion como agente

questions.prompt: Empareja cada ejemplo con el recurso figurativo que representa:

pairs.left: She's as sharp as a knife.
The stars danced in the sky.
I've told you a million times!

questions.explanation: Cinco recursos figurativos principales de la retorica anglo. Distinguirlos es fundamental en literary analysis (A-level, AP English, IB) y en escritura persuasiva. Hyperbole = exageracion deliberada consciente (no mentira, es efecto retorico). Onomatopeya = palabras que imitan sonidos (aparece en poesia y comics). Personificacion se distingue de metafora simple porque especificamente dota de agencia humana a lo no humano. Todos son universales en anglo global.
examples: Buzz of a bee, splash of a wave, hiss of a snake — pure onomatopoeia. → sonidos
The road stretched forever into the horizon — hyperbole giving epic scale. → exageracion narrativa

questions.target: Leadership is a marathon, not a sprint — you can't burn out at mile five and expect to finish strong.
questions.explanation: Metafora deportiva clasica del business ('marathon vs sprint'), combinada con dead metaphor 'burn out' (fuego). Estructura argumentativa fuerte: metafora + advertencia negativa + consecuencia. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'sprint —', enfasis fuerte en 'burn out' y 'finish strong'. Contracciones: 'can't' obligatoria. Registro: leadership/business, tipico de mentoring o keynote de management. Error hispano: traducir 'burn out' como 'quemarse' funciona en espanol coloquial reciente, pero en anglo es dead metaphor completamente naturalizada.
examples: Building a company is a marathon — pace yourself or you'll be limping by year two. → metafora sostenida
Life is like riding a bicycle — to keep your balance, you must keep moving. → simile de Einstein (atribuido)

questions.prompt: Una profesora describe su primer dia con estudiantes de 5 anos.
questions.question: 'The classroom was a zoo' is:
options: A literal description of animals in the room.
A metaphor comparing chaos to a zoo.
questions.explanation: Metafora clasica de caos: classroom AS zoo (animales sueltos, ruido, desorden). Efectiva porque evoca imagen inmediata sin necesidad de explicacion. Base del vivid descriptive writing en anglo. Colocacion tipica: 'X is a zoo/circus/madhouse/warzone' para describir caos. Registro: coloquial-conversacional, muy usado en anecdotas cotidianas (hospitales en pandemia, cocinas en hora punta, aeropuertos en Navidad).
examples: The office was a battlefield after the announcement — people arguing, doors slamming. → metafora belica
The airport was a circus this morning — three-hour queues everywhere. → metafora de caos organizado

questions.statement: Extended metaphors sustain the same figurative comparison across multiple sentences.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Extended metaphor = desarrollar una metafora inicial durante varias frases, manteniendo el mismo campo semantico. Ejemplo: 'Life is a chessboard...' seguido por 'moves', 'sacrifices', 'checkmate'. Recurso literario poderoso porque acumula profundidad conceptual: cada frase refuerza la metafora sin cambiar de imagen. Muy usado en TED talks (Simon Sinek), en poesia y en oratoria persuasiva. Registro: literario-elevado. Contrasta con mixed metaphors (mezclar campos) — error debilitador.
examples: The economy is a garden — some sectors bloom, others need pruning, and recessions are the winters we survive. → extended coherente
Learning is a river — it flows, it shapes us, and it never runs the same twice. → extended de progresion

questions.prompt: Estas en un pitch para inversores y el CEO habla del tiempo de vida de la empresa.
questions.question: In startup lingo, 'runway' is a metaphor for:
options: The paved surface at an airport.
The number of months before the company runs out of cash.
A pedestrian path through the city.
questions.explanation: 'Runway' en startup lingo = meses restantes de cash antes de bancarrota o siguiente ronda. Metafora del avion que despega: sin runway suficiente, no despegas. Ubicua en fundraising talk, VC pitches, board meetings. Colocacion: 'X months of runway', 'extend our runway', 'shorten the runway'. Registro: startup/VC exclusivo (en corporate tradicional no se usa asi). Error hispano: en muchas startups hispanoparlantes se anglosajoniza directamente ('tenemos 18 meses de runway'), no se traduce.
examples: We've got 18 months of runway at current burn — enough to hit profitability if we execute. → dato de fundraising
The Series B extended our runway to 2027, so we can focus on growth over survival. → alivio post-ronda

questions.text: The market is a battlefield right now — only the sharpest players will survive the next twelve months.
questions.explanation: Metafora belica clasica del business (MARKET IS WAR), con vocabulario coherente en el mismo campo semantico: 'battlefield', 'sharpest players', 'survive'. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'sharpest players' con /stp/ cluster consonantico dificil, la /t/ final tiende a elidirse dejando /ˈʃɑːrpəspleɪərz/. 'Right now' se enlaza como /raɪtnaʊ/. Colocaciones nativas: 'the market is a battlefield/warzone' es hyperbole legitimada; 'survive X months' comun en analisis competitivo. Registro: business analitico o motivacional.
examples: The startup arena is a war zone — casualties are inevitable, and most companies won't make it. → metafora dura
Every quarter is a new battle for market share, and yesterday's win means nothing today. → metafora recurrente

questions.prompt: En un discurso motivacional sobre educacion, el ponente usa la frase clave del cierre.
questions.question: 'Ideas planted seeds that grew into a movement' uses metaphor from:
questions.explanation: Metaforas de agriculture/gardening en anglo: 'plant a seed', 'grow', 'bear fruit', 'harvest', 'weed out', 'take root', 'flourish'. Muy comunes en discurso motivacional y educacional porque connotan crecimiento organico, paciencia, y transformacion positiva. Colocacion tipica: 'plant the seed of X' (una idea, una duda, una esperanza). Registro: motivacional-inspirational, comun en TED talks y conferencias educativas. Error hispano: existe equivalente 'plantar la semilla' — traduccion literal funciona.
examples: Small acts of kindness plant seeds we may never see grow — but they grow. → motivacional
That conversation with my mentor planted a seed that changed my whole career trajectory. → autobiografico

questions.statement: Mixed metaphors (combining incompatible images) usually strengthen persuasive writing.
questions.explanation: FALSO — al contrario, debilitan y a menudo provocan risa involuntaria. Mixed metaphor = combinar metaforas de campos semanticos incompatibles: 'let's grab the bull by the horns and hit the ground running' (toro + carrera son incompatibles). Suena ridiculo porque el cerebro intenta visualizar y falla. Regla de oro de la escritura persuasiva: elige UNA metafora y sostenla. Los editores buenos cazan mixed metaphors sin piedad. Error clasico: pensar que apilar idioms suena mas sofisticado — todo lo contrario.
examples: Weak (mixed): We need to nip this bull in the bud. → imagen imposible, provoca risa
Strong (coherent): We need to nip this in the bud before it spreads. → metafora vegetal sostenida

questions.target: Change is a river — you don't fight the current, you learn to navigate it, and eventually it takes you somewhere new.
questions.explanation: Extended metaphor completo de calidad TED: CHANGE IS A RIVER + 'fight the current' + 'navigate' + 'takes you somewhere'. Todo el vocabulario permanece en el mismo campo semantico (nautico/fluvial) — clave de la coherencia figurativa. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'river —', enfasis creciente en cada verbo, tono final ascendente en 'somewhere new'. Contracciones: 'don't' obligatoria. Registro: persuasivo-motivacional, tipico de coaching o cierre de charla. Recurso persuasivo TED-caliber.
examples: Time is a thief — you don't catch it, you just live with what it leaves behind. → extended metaphor filosofica
The mind is a garden — what you water grows, what you neglect withers. → metafora de responsabilidad personal
